newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 4.

text.p: PRAVO - On Monday, the crown broke through the 16.90 crown border with the German mark and traded at a record 16.865. Experts expect the strong crown to hold for a maximum of a few weeks.

- Today at midnight, railway workers began a strike which should last a minimum of 24 hours and has stopped all domestic and international railway transport. The railway workers union refused to call off the strike during meetings with Transport Minister Martin Riman yesterday.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - This year, SPT Telecom will reach an investment peak. While last year Telecom invested 30 billion crowns and in the previous year 20 billion crowns, its investment for this year will be approximately 32 billion crowns.

- After a meeting yesterday of the government fund for market regulation, Agriculture Minister Josef Lux confirmed that after this years harvest, the council has decided that the government will not import grain, but will place on the market 75,000 tonnes of wheat from its own supply and grain feed as a loan.

- Seven million crowns worth of medicines were supplied to General Faculty Hospital in Prague, which is in a financial crisis. A spokeswoman for the hospital stated that the medicines will last the hospital about seven to ten days.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The latest reports from the Czech Statistical Bureau show that the economy this year will grow at a rate of only four or five percent, which is less than all previous estimates.
- Demand for milk increased last year over 1995 by approximately 10 percent, which experts believe is caused by an increase in productivity in dairies.

- Bohumil Hrabal, one of the most well-known authors in the history of Czech literature, died tragically in Pragues Bulovka hospital yesterday. He accidentally fell from a window on the fifth floor orthopedic clinic where he was hospitalised.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The opposition Social Democratic Party (CSSD) should announce its position on changing the border with Slovakia. CSSDs approval will set conditions for meetings concerning individual compensation for citizens of U Sabotu which will be affected by the border change.
